problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=-3{e}^{5-x}$ at the point where $x=5-ln⁡(2).$
worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=-3{e}^{u},\,u=5-x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=-3{e}^{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1.
$$

We now apply the chain rule and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =-3{e}^{u}\cdot (-1) \\  & =3{e}^{u} \\  & =3{e}^{5-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the slope of the tangent to the curve at $x=5-ln⁡(2)$, we have to evaluate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}{|}_{x=5-ln⁡(2)} & =3{e}^{5-(5-ln⁡(2))} \\  & =3{e}^{ln⁡(2)} \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
